title.value: Distributional reinforcement learning with linear function approximation
title.justification: The title is present at the beginning of the paper and consistently referenced throughout the document.
title.quote: Distributional reinforcement learning with linear function approximation

analysis.description: The paper proposes a new distributional reinforcement learning algorithm that is fully based on the Cramér distance. It adapts the Cramér distance for arbitrary vectors and combines linear function approximation with theoretical guarantees in the scope of policy evaluation. The research suggests that while the new algorithm converges under standard conditions, it may perform worse than direct value function approximation.

type.justification: The paper focuses on theoretical analysis and proofs for the behavior of distributional reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly those based on the Cramér distance, rather than empirical studies or experiments.
type.quote: This new algorithm enables us to derive theoretical guarantees on the behaviour of a distributional algorithm when combined to linear function approximation, in the policy evaluation setting.
